name: Muong Hoa valley: Lao Chai to Ta Van
region: Mường Hoa valley, Sa Pa, Lào Cai
why: The classic Sa Pa walk: on the dykes of the rice terraces down the Muong Hoa valley, from the Hmong village of Lao Chai to the Giay village of Ta Van.
book: No permit. Take a taxi or motorbike from Sa Pa to Lao Chai and arrange a pick-up at the Ta Van bridge, or join a guided village walk. Local Hmong guides can be hired in Sa Pa; the women offering to guide you in Lao Chai can be insistent.
water: Drinks and lunch in Lao Chai and Ta Van, where most homestays serve food. Carry 1 litre.
dangers: Paddy dykes and clay paths are muddy and slippery after rain: wear shoes with good grip.
Motorbikes on the valley road: walk on its edge where the trail joins it.
Thick fog and cold from November to February.
turnaround: No hard turnaround: the road along the valley links both villages if you want to stop.

points.name: Lao Chai rice terraces
points.note: The Black Hmong village on the slopes of the valley, about 8 km below Sa Pa. The terraces are green in July and August, golden in September and early October.

points.name: Muong Hoa river terraces
points.note: The path follows the dykes of the paddies along the south bank of the river, with Fansipan's ridge behind on clear days.

points.name: Ta Van village
points.note: The Giay village by the river, full of homestays and cafes. Cross the bridge to the road for the ride back to Sa Pa.
